text:
maria: Noticed a regression on host-side tail for small requests. p95 up ~18% on staging during short spikes. Putting initial traces here.

aj: Which code paths are hot? tokenization, parsing, or decode?

maria: Parsing + streaming framer. pprof flame shows parse_and_route -> stream_writer -> writev as hot spots at the tail. decode/generation unaffected.

todd: Any kernel picker flips around the same time? If the runtime chooses the fallback kernel it can increase per-token CPU and change batching behavior.

maria: Yup, enabled kernel-picker debug: when parallelism is low and seq variance high, it picks the generic kernel (slow path). That lowers effective batch consolidation and we see more small RPC writes.

anya: Could be a combined effect: slow kernel -> smaller kv cache hit window -> more evictions. Do we have eviction telemetry?

maria: Enabled kvcache debug and captured traces. Eviction rate spikes correlate with the bursts. Hot prefixes get evicted, then subsequent requests miss and trigger more parsing work.

aj: Can you share a quick repro client? I'll run it and collect writev counts.

maria: Repro (bash):

```
# burst repro
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  for j in $(seq 1 25); do
    curl -sS -X POST http://staging:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"hey"}' &
  done
  wait
  sleep 0.06
done
```

Works reliably for me.

todd: Observed the framer issuing ~4-8 small writev syscalls per response during the bursts. Syscall overhead adds ~90-150us per request on avg.

anya: Two low-risk interventions: 1) coalesce framer writes up to 1KB or until a 2ms timer; 2) bump min_batch heuristic so optimized kernel stays chosen for short seqs (e.g., prefer optimized kernel if estimated_batch >=2 and seq_len <=96).

aj: Coalesce patch seems safe; streaming semantics tests cover flush/timers. Kernel threshold change needs perf validation to avoid regressions on long sequences.

maria: Also propose a transient kvcache TTL increase when we detect microburst mode to avoid churn. TTL bump for 5s windows when eviction rate > threshold.

todd: Good idea. We should add a metric "microburst_mode" and emit why kernel-picker chose fallback (reasons).

perf-bot: Kicking perf run: job=perf/5791-framer-coalesce. A/B: baseline vs framer-coalesce+ttl-bump. ETA ~40m.

maria: I'll land framer coalesce as a hotfix behind a feature flag. Kernel heuristic changes behind a runtime flag after perf pass.

aj: Running repro and collecting traces now; will attach writev counter + kvcache evict log here.

perf-bot: job perf/5791-framer-coalesce finished. Summary: p95 reduced 12% in burst traffic; writev syscalls per response down 57%; kvcache evictions down 36%. Full artifacts in perf dashboard.

maria: Nice. Merge coalesce hotfix to staging and start gradual rollout. Keep kernel changes behind flag pending longer-run perf.

todd: Filing follow-ups: add "fallback-reason" telemetry, microburst detector, and an e2e test simulating small burst patterns (ENG-RT-203).

maria: Filed ENG-RT-203 and ENG-OPT-210 for kernel heuristic canary. Closing this triage unless we see regressions on long sequences. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
